author: swain
title: Run the agent dispatch crons as pg-boss schedules that fan out per record
body:
The Serve and Win agent dispatchers ran as `@Cron` jobs on every gp-api task, deduped by `cron_run` claims, and each looped over every office, org or campaign in one pass. A record that failed was logged and skipped: no retry, no alert, and nobody knew a briefing, community-issue list, ordinance refresh, opponent refresh, tracker regeneration, managed panel wave or round 2 draw had not happened until a user noticed. The round 2 draw and the managed panel waves spend real texts, so a silent skip there costs money or a send day.

This moves the nine crons in these seven services onto pg-boss schedules (ADR `2026-11-07-scheduled-jobs-on-pg-boss-schedules`). Each schedule finds its records and fans out one job per record with `sendMany`, so one bad office retries, dead-letters and pages on its own while the rest run. pg-boss sends one job per occurrence, so the `cron_run` claims go.

Pacing: the briefing and community-issue crons ran 10 offices at a time with no sleeps, and the agent platform queues the runs itself. Their per-record jobs keep that fleet-wide with `maxConcurrent: 10` (2 per task). Opponent research re-dispatched one row at a time, so its job has `maxConcurrent: 1`. Ordinance refresh and tracker regeneration were serial only by accident of the loop (their comments say the agent platform paces them), so they run 2 per task with no fleet cap. The caps that bound paid runs per day (200 community-issue orgs, 200 opponent rows, one row per campaign) stay in the fan-out. The round 2 draw runs one at a time per task, since each draw is a Databricks sample and a model fit. Managed panel jobs are grouped by panel so two runs of one panel never overlap, as the hourly lock guaranteed before.

Times that move because pg-boss crons are UTC only. Each runs an hour later in local time while daylight saving is on:

- Round 2 draw (`priorityRoundTwoDrawDue`): `41 12 * * *` UTC, 7:41 AM Eastern in winter, 8:41 AM in summer (was 7:41 AM Eastern all year).
- Campaign tracker weekly regeneration (`campaignTrackerWeekly`): Thursday `0 15 * * 4` UTC, 9 AM Central in winter, 10 AM in summer (was 9 AM Central all year).

The managed panel waves stay at :19 past every hour. The briefing, community-issue, ordinance and opponent schedules were already UTC and keep their times.

Behavior a reviewer should know:

- A per-record failure now retries, then dead-letters and pages through `jobs-dead-letter`. Before, it was logged and retried the next day. That covers an election-api resolve that times out on the ordinance refresh too.
- Each managed panel not stopped gets one job per hourly run that takes its wave step, then its confirmation text if due, then its milestones, so a panel that fills gets its thank-you text in the same run. A failure in any of them retries and dead-letters for that panel alone.
- A scheduled opponent re-dispatch whose dispatch fails now hands its row back and fails the job, so it retries and pages; a deploy with no agent queue, or a test-user org, still completes quietly.
- A managed panel job that retries after its confirmation text was claimed never texts again: only an unclaimed confirmation is picked up, and `claimConfirmationFree` commits the claim before it enqueues.
- `managedPanelWaveAdvance` reaches `claimFree`. Only the schedule sends it, and the managed panel AGENTS.md says no request may.
- `serve-managed-panel-wave-failed` no longer matches a failed step: the step's own job now retries and pages through `jobs-dead-letter`. It still pages on a failed Slack notice, which does not throw.
- `jobs.test.ts` now checks the pgboss queues and schedules against `JOBS` and `SCHEDULES` instead of a hand-kept list, so each port no longer has to edit it (and conflict with the others).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches paid agent dispatches, managed panel free texts, and round-2 draws—failures now retry/DLQ instead of silent daily skip, and UTC schedule shifts change when some jobs run locally during DST.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces nine NestJS `@Cron` + `CronLockService` dispatch loops (meeting briefings, community issues, ordinance refresh, opponent research, campaign tracker weekly, managed civic panel waves, priority round-2 draw, and related paths) with **pg-boss schedules** that enqueue **one job per office/org/campaign/panel/send**, keyed by day or run so duplicate schedule firings do not double-send.
> 
> **Operational changes:** per-record failures **retry and dead-letter** (and page via `jobs-dead-letter`) instead of being logged and skipped until the next cron day. Concurrency caps mirror the old behavior where it mattered (`maxConcurrent: 10` for briefing/community-issue fan-out, `maxConcurrent: 1` for opponent research). Managed panels use `managedPanelWaveAdvance` jobs **grouped by panel**; each job runs wave step, optional confirmation text, then milestones in one unit. Round-2 draw moves to UTC `41 12 * * *` (Eastern local time shifts with DST); campaign tracker weekly moves to Thursday `0 15 * * 4` UTC.
> 
> **Supporting updates:** `CronModule` dropped from affected Nest modules; `jobs.registry.ts` registers new workers and schedules; tests switch to `useTestService({ jobs: true })` and `runSchedule`; Grafana alert `serve-managed-panel-wave-failed` no longer pages on thrown wave steps (those go through job DLQ); docs and legacy cron lint lists updated; `jobs.test.ts` asserts queues/schedules from `JOBS`/`SCHEDULES` dynamically.
>
